title: Choosing Between Request/Response and Event-Driven Communication
objective: Model the same workflow under synchronous and event-driven communication, and record a decision that names its delivery-guarantee assumption.
whyThisMatters: The choice between synchronous coupling and asynchronous events determines who owns failure. Picking one without stating the delivery-guarantee assumption is how 'we'll process the event eventually' turns into a silent data-loss bug six months later.
evidence: Two sequence or flow diagrams, one per communication style, modeling the same workflow end to end
An ADR naming the ordering and delivery-guarantee assumption made for the chosen style
A note walking through at least one concrete failure scenario for the rejected style and why it was rejected
acceptanceCriteria: Both diagrams model the same workflow end to end, not two different scopes.
The ADR explicitly states the delivery-guarantee assumption (at-least-once, at-most-once, or an explained approximation of exactly-once) for the chosen style.
At least one concrete failure scenario is walked through for the rejected style, explaining why it was rejected rather than merely less preferred.
